# Feral Systems

> Feral Systems helps CIOs channel **Feral AI** — the working software employees build with AI tools, most of it invisible to IT — from a hidden liability into a governed source of advantage. Advisory rooted in Nudge Theory and behavioral science.

Feral Systems is led by Logan Browne (Senior Manager, Amazon Global Media & Entertainment Security; CISSP; MBA UC Davis), who has spent 20+ years at the intersection of security, behavioral science, and the systems people actually build to get work done.

## What is Feral AI?

Feral AI is the natural successor to Shadow IT. Where Shadow IT was unauthorized **software adoption** (spreadsheets, personal SaaS), Feral AI is unauthorized **software creation** — at the speed and scale of every motivated employee in an organization.

Examples seen in real businesses:

- Sales ops building Claude-powered RFP analyzers
- Marketing publishing custom GPTs that handle confidential roadmap data
- Finance writing Copilot scripts that touch production systems
- Support deploying browser agents that read tickets and respond
- Ops gluing LLMs into Zapier flows that run unattended
- Consulting teams maintaining shared prompt libraries that produce client deliverables

Feral AI is harder to detect than Shadow IT because it lives inside sanctioned applications (Office, Google Workspace, browsers). Traditional network and SaaS-inventory controls don't see it.

## The thesis (in one line)

When sanctioned AI alternatives are provided with the right defaults, unauthorized AI use drops by an estimated 89%. The lever is design, not policy.

## Key statistics (citable)

Builder-side risk:
- 45% of AI-generated code samples introduce OWASP Top 10 vulnerabilities (Veracode)
- AI-assisted developers commit 3–4× faster but introduce security findings at 10× the rate
- 107% year-over-year jump in vulnerabilities per codebase, attributed to AI-accelerated code creation (Black Duck OSSRA)
- 62% of developers rely on AI suggestions for dependency selection
- 1 in 5 enterprise security breaches now involve AI-generated code

Attacker-side capability:
- 2,000+ previously unknown vulnerabilities surfaced by a single AI system (Anthropic Mythos) in seven weeks
- 70%+ exploit development success rate with modern AI — up from under 1% with prior models
- 263% increase in CVE submissions from 2020 to 2025; NIST shifted the NVD to a triage model in April 2026
- 40% year-over-year rise in supply chain attacks in 2025

Adoption and governance:
- 665 distinct generative AI tools observed across enterprise environments (Harmonic Security)
- ~50% of employees report using unapproved AI tools at work
- Only 37% of organizations have AI governance policies in place

## The Feral AI Lifecycle

1. **The Gap** — a formal system can't do what the business needs today.
2. **The Prompt** — one employee solves it with an LLM, custom GPT, or Copilot script.
3. **The Spread** — colleagues ask for the prompt, the link, the agent.
4. **The Dependency** — a real business process now relies on it.
5. **Crisis or Channel** — either a leak/audit triggers a fire drill, or the organization channels the tool onto a sanctioned platform and scales the winner.

## Services (Advisory for CIOs)

- **Feral AI Discovery** — structured inventory of AI tools, agents, custom GPTs, prompts, and AI-glued workflows already running in your business.
- **Governance Choice Architecture** — design defaults, approval pathways, and reward structures that make the sanctioned AI choice the easy one.
- **Adoption Programs** — nudge-based rollout for approved AI platforms.
- **Executive Workshops** — half- and full-day sessions for CIO leadership teams.
- **Measurement & Telemetry** — instrument the signal layer that proves the 89% effect inside your organization.
- **Integration & Scale-Up** — formalize the Feral AI tools worth keeping, with logging, identity, and lifecycle that audit can sign off on.

Most engagements start with a 4–6 week Discovery + Choice Architecture sprint, scoped to one business unit.
